Statistics


How to Play


Raise a realm, climb through four Ages and destroy every rival banner. Each race has its own look, bonuses and a unique Citadel unit.


MOUSE & CAMERA
  • Left click / drag select · double-click selects all of a type on screen
  • Right click context order: move, attack, gather, build, repair · with a building selected it sets the rally point
  • Scroll the map: push the mouse against any screen edge (top and bottom too) · Arrow keys · Shift scrolls faster · Middle drag or hold Space + left drag to grab the map
  • Zoom: Wheel zooms smoothly toward your cursor · PgUp / PgDn · on a trackpad, two-finger scroll pans and pinch zooms (auto-detected; switch in the Menu)
  • Minimap: left-click jumps, right-click orders · Home centres on your Town Center


KEYBOARD
  • The command card uses the grid keys Q W E R T / A S D F G / Z X C V B — the letter is shown on each button. Shift trains five units or keeps placing buildings.
  • Ctrl+1…9 set a group · 1…9 recall (twice centres) · . / , idle villagers · H Town Center · tap Space last alert · Del delete · + / − game speed · Esc menu


THE BASICS
  • Shrine, Monks and Acolytes (Bronze Age): build a Shrine, then right-click it with villagers. A villager who prays there 5 times becomes a Monk (he still gathers and builds). Once you have a Monk, research Acolyte Rites at the Shrine and it can train Acolytes, stronger Monks. Wounded units can also right-click a Shrine to pray for healing, one at a time.
  • Temple, Priests and Priestesses (Silver Age): only Monks and Acolytes can build a Temple (select one, then Build Economic). It trains Priests and Priestesses. When idle they heal the most wounded friend nearby. They fight back only if attacked and never chase, so keep them behind your army.
  • Sacred groves, the Sacred Tree and the Heart Tree (Silver Age): every map has sacred groves (3 on Small to Large maps, 4 on Huge, 5 on Giant and Colossal), rings of standing stones with an altar in the middle (shown on the minimap). Nobody can attack, or be attacked, inside one, and nothing can be built there. Only a Priestess can receive a sacred seed: press Fetch Sacred Seed (or right-click the altar stone) and she stands at the altar for 10 seconds. Then press Plant Sacred Tree and click a clear spot outside the grove. If she falls with the seed it drops where she died, and any Priestess, yours or an enemy's, can pick it up. Monks, Acolytes, Priests and Priestesses water the tree: select them and press Carry Water (or right-click the tree). They scoop water from any water tile and carry it back. After 35 waterings it becomes the Heart Tree: far stronger than a Citadel, it shoots arrows, and your King and up to 10 other units can shelter inside and heal (right-click it with them; press Bring Everyone Out to let them out). If a growing tree is destroyed, its waterings are lost and you need a new seed. A Priestess can take a new seed from any Sacred Tree or Heart Tree you own.
  • Heart Tree, Healing Fountains, Druids, High Priests and High Priestesses: once you own a Sacred Tree you can build Healing Fountains (Build Economic), which heal every friendly unit around them. The Heart Tree trains three units. Druids (Silver Age) heal like Priests and can befriend wild animals and magical creatures: press Befriend and click one, or right-click it, and after 6 seconds it is yours for good and takes no population space. High Priests (Gold Age) grant epic blessings to the soldiers within 9 tiles for 25 seconds: Kinship (stronger the more comrades stand close), Last Stand (wounded soldiers hit harder and faster) and Quickening (faster attacks). They need 40 seconds between blessings. High Priestesses (Gold Age) are the only units that convert: press Convert and click an enemy soldier or villager (or right-click him) and she channels for 20 seconds within 6 tiles, then rests a few seconds. Converted units stay with you for good. Kings, siege and boats cannot be converted, and nothing works inside a sacred grove.
  • Shepherds, the Shepherd's Hut and the Creamery (Bronze Age): build a Shepherd's Hut and right-click it with villagers. A villager who works there 4 times becomes a Shepherd (he still gathers and builds). Only a Shepherd can build a Creamery, a dairy with a fenced pen. Select a Shepherd, press Herd (or right-click a cow, goat or sheep) and he wins the animal over, leads it to a Creamery and sends it into the pen (6 animals fit). Each penned animal feeds one Shepherd: right-click the Creamery with Shepherds and they gather rich, never-ending dairy food and carry it home like any other food. The Creamery is a food drop-off, and its upgrades (Butter Churn, Cheese Press, Yogurt Crocks) make dairy food flow faster. Fished-out fish shoals now hold twice as much and slowly fill again.
  • Villagers gather food (berries, farms), wood, gold and stone. Drop-off buildings near resources make them far more efficient.
  • Stances (command card, D): Aggressive chases anything, Defensive fights nearby then returns, Stand Ground only fires in range, Passive never fights. Idle soldiers also rush to help a friend or building that is attacked.
  • Defeat: you fall when your last Town Center or Citadel does, unless a villager raises a new one within 90 seconds. Stray houses and hiding villagers no longer matter. The Stats button shows the full statistics screen at any time.
  • Hunting & fishing: right-click a deer, stag, goat, cow, sheep, hare or pheasant with villagers (or soldiers) to bring it down, and the villagers then gather the carcass automatically. Boars, wolves and bears fight back, so send an army. Right-click a school of fish from the shore to fish. Food goes to your Town Center or Mill, so build a Mill near good hunting.
  • Transports & islands: from the Bronze Age a Dock also trains a Transport that carries up to 10 land troops (cavalry count 2, siege 3). Right-click the transport with soldiers or villagers to board, sail beside a shore and press Unload (or right-click a shore spot with the loaded transport selected). A sunk transport spills its troops onto nearby land, or loses them at sea. Pick Islands under Land in the lobby to start every player on their own island. The Dock also researches boat upgrades (nets, hulls, sails, sights), and the computer builds docks, fishes, and ferries its army across the water.
  • Walls & gates: from the Bronze Age villagers can build Stone Walls (Build Military): click and drag to lay a line, release to place it. Press Tab while placing to change the shape: straight, straight with rounded towers, a curve (either way round), or a round wall (press at the centre and drag out to the radius). Pieces join up automatically. A Gate lets your own units walk straight through but is a wall to everyone else; place it on a spot in your wall (it replaces a wall piece). Soldiers who are sent to attack something behind a wall will hack their way through, and rams and catapults are fastest. Arrows barely scratch stone.
  • Market & trade: the Market (Build Economic, Bronze Age) lets you buy and sell 100 food, wood or stone for gold at a time (hold Shift for 500). Every deal nudges that price against you and it drifts back to normal over time. In the Silver Age a Market trains Caravans: with two markets, a caravan walks between them and earns gold on every trip, more the farther apart they are. Right-click a market with a caravan to send it. Markets (and docks) must be at least 10 tiles apart for a trip to pay. Caravans carry no weapons, so guard the road. With two Docks on the same water, a Dock trains Market Boats (Silver Age) that sail between them and earn gold the same way.
  • Regicide: pick it under Victory in the lobby. Every realm starts with a free Citadel and a King who begins the game safe inside it. If your King falls your realm falls at once. Right-click a Town Center, Citadel or Watch Tower with him selected (or press his Garrison button) and he steps inside, where he heals and cannot be hit; press Bring Out King on the building to let him out. To reach a hidden King, destroy the building he is in.
  • Docks & boats: villagers can build a Dock on a lake shore (it needs at least 8 tiles of water beside it). It trains a Fishing Boat (right-click a fish shoal; the catch is carried to a Dock) and, from the Bronze Age, a ranged War Boat. Every realm sails its own kind of boat. Boats stay on the water; soldiers without bows cannot hit them, but towers and archers can.
  • Build houses to raise your population cap. Research ages at the Town Center once you own two buildings of the current age.
  • Pikemen beat cavalry, cavalry beats archers, archers beat infantry, mages ignore physical armor, rams and catapults break buildings.
  • AI difficulty ranks Easy < Normal < Hard < BATTLE ON — the last one gathers faster, starts richer and attacks early.
